page: Amazon Web Services c9g.metal-48xl is a bare-metal compute-optimized server powered by AWS Graviton processors based on the ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 architecture. It features 192 dedicated physical cores and 192 vCPUs running at 3.3 GHz, with a 1:1 core-to-thread topology. The CPU architecture integrates 64 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and a large 96 MB L3 cache per socket configuration, alongside hardware AES support. The system delivers 384.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory, maintaining a 1:2 compute-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. There is no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage options, and zero integrated GPUs are included. Network baseline throughput is configured at 100 Gbps.

Benchmark results highlight extreme multi-threaded capability and massive memory bandwidth. The instance achieves top-tier results in stress-ng multi-core testing (383,027.58) and PassMark CPU ratings (108,106.68), accompanied by 726.85 GB/sec uncached read and 339.15 GB/sec uncached write DDR5 bandwidth. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches 1,914.52 GB/sec, Clang compilation scores 113,438.0, and Redis SET throughput delivers 520.74 million operations per second. Static web serving throughput also places in the top tier at 351.23 GB/sec. However, single-core stress-ng performance and Geekbench image processing fall within median percentiles, while small LLM text generation shows lower efficiency compared to GPU-accelerated configurations.

The c9g.metal-48xl offers strong qualitative cost efficiency for scaled multi-core workloads by providing 192 full physical ARM cores without hyperthreading penalties. The absence of local NVMe storage requires architectural consideration for IOPS-bound setups relying on network storage. This bare-metal platform is suited for large-scale distributed compilation, high-concurrency Redis caching, parallel scientific computation, massive batch data compression, and high-throughput static web serving fleets.

Configured without simultaneous multithreading, it provides 192 dedicated vCPUs alongside 384.0 GB of DDR5 memory, reflecting a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio. It lacks integrated local storage and GPUs, but features a 100 Gbps baseline network interface. In benchmarks, the server demonstrates top-tier multi-core computing, exceptional uncached DDR5 memory bandwidth exceeding 700 GB/sec, and high-throughput capabilities in software compilation, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and Redis operations. The platform trades off bundled local storage for massive raw CPU and network throughput. It is technically suited for large-scale parallel build systems, high-density in-memory caching, static web traffic handling, and compute-intensive batch processing workloads.
